original_test_intent: Demonstrate that two correctable errors on the same intended GNR DRAM row reach the configured software threshold, cause BIOS to qualify that row, persist a boot-time Soft PPR request and complete repair with nonzero DramMask evidence.
original_method: Record platform/DIMM topology, harness and BIOS baseline; map every source PPR/fast-boot/threshold knob and exact socket0/channel0/subchannel0/DIMM0/rank0/subrank0/bankgroup0/bank0/ps_ch0 row; preserve logs; execute only the approved memDevs setup and first CE, prove 1/2 plus extlog; execute the second identical CE, prove threshold reached, row qualification and extmem; run one approved `itp.resettarget`, retain continuous serial evidence through boot, correlate the same row and nonzero DramMask/PprRepairStatus, verify health, and restore settings.
manual_activity: Intel-qualified owner/FAE validates the sacrificial row, controls the two injections and reset/recovery; the agent may correlate serial, FTrace, PPR and health evidence.

review_improvement: Restores the exact two-stage threshold and boot repair chain that generic logs omitted, with same-row identity, persistence, reset and recovery controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: Boot-time PPR is causal across a reset: two events must hit one row, the second must cross the configured threshold, firmware must persist that row in NVRAM and the next boot must repair that same row. Evidence from either injection alone or an unrelated nonzero DramMask cannot prove the chain. The exact coordinate, stage-specific serial/ELog records and reset continuity are therefore mandatory; extra injections would change the threshold experiment and are prohibited.
